title: Cross-team SLI Burn-rate Dashboard and Rollback Policy for Reliability Initiatives
creator: Ethan Liu
description:
Goal: Ship a cross-team SLI burn-rate dashboard and formalize a rollback policy that ties into the Redwood Console rollouts and the incident playbook. The dashboard should show per-initiative and per-service burn rate, projected exhaustion time for error budgets, recent SLI trends, and highlight anomalies. The rollback policy should define automated and manual escalation thresholds, owner handoffs, and links to runbook actions.

Why this matters: Teams are currently reacting to SLO breaches with ad-hoc interventions. We need a single place to see which initiatives are consuming error budget fastest, make informed canary/rollout decisions, and perform consistent rollbacks to protect customer experience and SLAs.

This ticket covers product design, requirements for the Console UI, backend SLI aggregation requirements, alerting rules, and the initial guardrails for automated rollback integration with the rollout engine.
background: During Q4 2025 multiple services exceeded SLI thresholds in short bursts. Post-incident review showed inconsistent measurements across teams, no shared view of burn rate, and ambiguity about when to abort a rollout. Current console shows token-level latency/cost charts but lacks unified SLI burn-rate telemetry per initiative. This increases outage risk and slows mitigation. The intended outcome is a reliable indicator that drives faster, standardized decisions across PM/Eng/Oncall.
acceptance_criteria: A Grafana-like dashboard integrated into Redwood Console showing per-service and per-initiative burn rate with projected exhaustion time (24h/72h horizons)
Dashboard filters: time-range, environment (prod/staging), model variant, and rollout ID
Burn-rate calculation documented and consistent with SLO definitions and queryable in our metrics store
Two alert tiers configured: warning (50% projected in X hours) and critical (100% projected in Y hours) with Slack and PagerDuty hooks
Rollback policy document published and wired into rollout engine with a canary abort trigger when burn-rate crosses critical threshold
Playbook steps added to incident runbooks and a one-click rollback action available to oncall in Console
tasks: Design: wireframes for burn-rate panel and rollback controls
Engineering: implement burn-rate aggregation job and expose metrics via metrics API
Console: embed burn-rate visuals and rollout abort button
Alerts: create templated alert rules and Slack/PagerDuty integrations
Docs: publish rollback policy, calculation formulas, and runbook updates
Pilot: run a 2-week pilot with Payment Platform and Search teams
decisions: Use a rolling-window approach (error budget spent / error budget window) for burn-rate rather than instantaneous rate to reduce noise
Critical threshold = projected exhaustion within 4 hours; Warning = projected exhaustion within 24 hours (subject to pilot tuning)
Automated abort only for canary rollouts at critical threshold; for broader rollouts trigger an immediate paging and lock the rollout for manual review
Metric source: canonical SLI vectors in metrics-store (avoid local service-level aggregates to prevent discrepancies)
